**4B.2 Research Note**
**Working verdict:** **mixed, leaning no**. I found little direct evidence that Marcos personally rewrote election law, captured courts, or openly bent Comelec in 2024. But I did find repeated evidence of red-tagging, media pressure, disinformation management, and security-adjacent intimidation that can serve incumbent entrenchment even when formal election rules stay intact.

| Direction | Claim-level item | Source | Date | URL | QIDs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mixed / positive | Marcos told critics to let Comelec handle allegations that signatures in the people’s initiative drive may have been bought. That is a small sign of deference to the election commission rather than direct executive interference. | GMA News Online | 2024-01-23 | https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/895067/marcos-on-people-s-initiative-for-cha-cha-let-comelec-do-their-job/story/ | 4B.2, 4B.1 |
| Mixed / positive | Marcos publicly pledged a free and safe environment for journalists and said critical press is better than a compliant press. This is not proof of practice, but it cuts against overt media capture rhetoric. | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-15 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-declares-free-safe-environment-for-journalists-under-bagong-pilipinas/ | 4B.2, 4B.1, 3B.8, 3B.3 |
| Mixed / positive | After a deepfake video, the government said DICT and the NSC were investigating and considering legal action. That is a reactive legal response, not a censorship or emergency-power sweep. | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-04-26 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/govt-vows-legal-action-vs-deep-fake-video-creators-spreaders/ | 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.6 |
| Mixed / positive | The administration expanded eFOI access and kept a media-literacy / disinformation campaign in place. That supports a limited transparency posture rather than outright information closure. | Philippine News Agency | 2024-01-18 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1217036 | 4B.2, 3B.6, 3B.8 |
| Mixed / positive | PCO said it would place fact-check officers in state media and denied any policy or practice of red-tagging in the Marcos administration. This is a real formal anti-disinformation step, though not a full safeguard against abuse. | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-09-09 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pco-to-designate-fact-check-officers-in-state-media-to-fight-fake-news/ | 4B.2, 3B.3, 3B.8 |
| Mixed / positive | Marcos pushed procurement reform to shorten timelines, standardize forms, and institutionalize e-procurement. That is evidence against using public resources primarily as a personal patronage machine. | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-07-20 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/pbbm-signs-laws-on-streamlining-procurement-combatting-online-scams/ | 4B.2, 3B.10 |
| Mixed / positive | Marcos reorganized the National Security Council to make it a more resilient institution and improve coordination. The structure is institutional rather than purely loyalist, though it still centralizes presidential discretion. | Lawphil / Office of the President | 2024-12-30 | https://lawphil.net/executive/execord/eo2024/eo_81_2024.html | 4B.2, 3B.9, 3B.10 |
| Negative | Freedom House says Philippine elections are free from overt restrictions but not fully fair because disinformation and vote buying distort competition; it also says red-tagging persisted under Marcos. This is the strongest broad external warning against clean non-entrenchment. | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/philippines/freedom-world/2024 | 4B.2, 4B.1, 3B.3, 3B.8 |
| Negative | HRW said red-tagging under Marcos placed leftist activists and critics at serious risk, with officials and supporters accusing them of communist ties. That is consistent with intimidation of opposition space rather than neutral competition. | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk | 4B.2, 4B.1, 3B.3, 3B.8 |
| Negative | HRW reported Marcos-era officials and police or military members repeatedly visited union leaders and threatened them by linking them to communism. This is direct evidence of coercive pressure on civic organization. | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-25 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders | 4B.2, 3B.8, 3B.7 |
| Negative | Amnesty says Marcos-era actors weaponized digital tools, misinformation, and the anti-terror law to create fear, and that red-tagging vilified activists, journalists, teachers, and others. That undercuts a claim of cleanly fair competition. | Amnesty International | 2024-10-14 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8574/2024/en/ | 4B.2, 4B.1, 3B.3, 3B.8 |
| Negative | The Reuters Institute report says red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats against journalists persisted under Marcos. That indicates a coercive information environment that can advantage incumbents. | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines | 4B.2, 4B.1, 3B.3, 3B.8 |
| Negative | The U.S. State Department report says credible killings, disappearances, torture, arbitrary detention, media restrictions, and threats to labor activists remained. That is not consistent with a fully neutral, non-entrenching governing environment. | U.S. State Department via ecoi.net | 2024 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128580.html | 4B.2, 3B.10, 3B.8, 3B.1 |

**Bottom line:** I did not find strong 2024 evidence of explicit electoral-rule manipulation or direct Comelec/court capture. But the evidence does support a finding that Marcos did **not** fully refrain from other entrenchment-friendly tactics, especially red-tagging, media pressure, and coercive information management.

**Search gap:** I did not find a clean 2024 case showing Marcos personally rewrote election rules, ordered election-commission manipulation, or used courts to disqualify opponents. The record is stronger on indirect entrenchment and civic intimidation than on formal electoral fraud.
